questions.text: The fundamental economic problem facing every society is
options: scarcity of resources relative to wants
questions.explanation: Economics exists because wants are unlimited while the resources to satisfy them are limited.

questions.text: The real cost of a chosen alternative measured in terms of the next best alternative forgone is
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost expresses what must be given up whenever a scarce resource is committed to one use.

questions.text: An increase in the price of a commodity, other things being equal, will lead to
questions.explanation: The law of demand states an inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded, shown as a movement along the curve.

questions.text: If a 10% fall in price raises quantity demanded by 20%, the price elasticity of demand is
questions.explanation: Ed = %ΔQ ÷ %ΔP = 20/10 = 2, and any value above 1 is elastic.

questions.text: The reward for the factor of production known as entrepreneurship is
questions.explanation: Land earns rent, labour earns wages, capital earns interest and the entrepreneur earns profit for bearing risk.

questions.text: The law of diminishing returns operates in the
options: long run when all factors are variable
short run when at least one factor is fixed
long run when the scale of production changes
short run when all factors are variable
questions.explanation: Adding more of a variable factor to a fixed factor eventually reduces the marginal product, which is a short-run phenomenon.

questions.text: A market in which there are many sellers of differentiated products is known as
questions.explanation: Monopolistic competition combines many sellers with product differentiation and free entry.

questions.text: The principal function of a central bank is to
options: issue currency and regulate the banking system
questions.explanation: The central bank is the currency-issuing authority, banker to government and regulator of commercial banks.

questions.text: Inflation caused by a persistent rise in the cost of raw materials and wages is described as
questions.explanation: Cost-push inflation originates from the supply side as higher production costs are passed on to consumers.

questions.text: Gross national product minus capital consumption allowance gives
questions.explanation: Deducting depreciation (capital consumption) from GNP gives net national product.

questions.text: A tax whose rate rises as the income of the taxpayer rises is
questions.explanation: Progressive taxation takes a larger percentage of higher incomes, as in personal income tax bands.

questions.text: A situation where the value of a country's visible imports exceeds that of its visible exports is called
questions.explanation: The balance of trade covers visible items only; an excess of imports over exports is unfavourable, that is, a trade deficit.

questions.text: A population is said to be optimum when
options: it is the largest the country can feed
it combines with available resources to give the highest output per head
the birth rate equals the death rate
questions.explanation: Optimum population maximises output per head given the country's resources and technology.

questions.text: A major disadvantage of a sole proprietorship is
questions.explanation: The owner's personal assets can be used to settle business debts because the business has no separate legal personality.

questions.text: A marketing board performs all of the following functions except
options: fixing the exchange rate of the naira
questions.explanation: Exchange rate policy belongs to the central bank, not to commodity marketing boards.

questions.text: In a free market economy, resources are allocated mainly through
questions.explanation: Prices act as signals that guide producers and consumers in what the market calls the invisible hand.

questions.text: Equilibrium price in a competitive market is determined where
questions.explanation: Market clearing occurs at the intersection of the demand and supply curves.

questions.text: Two commodities that are consumed together, such as bread and butter, are described as
questions.explanation: Complementary goods are in joint demand, so a rise in the price of one reduces demand for the other.

questions.text: The additional satisfaction derived from consuming one more unit of a commodity is called
questions.explanation: Marginal utility is the change in total utility from consuming an extra unit, and it falls as consumption rises.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a function of money?
questions.explanation: Money facilitates exchange but is not itself a factor of production; land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship are.

questions.text: A budget in which government proposed expenditure exceeds expected revenue is
questions.explanation: A deficit budget is often used deliberately to stimulate an economy in recession.

questions.text: Unemployment caused by a fall in demand during a downturn in the business cycle is
questions.explanation: Cyclical unemployment rises in recession and falls during recovery as aggregate demand returns.

questions.text: The liability of shareholders in a public limited company is limited to
options: the amount unpaid on their shares
the value of the company's assets
questions.explanation: Limited liability restricts a shareholder's loss to what they agreed to pay for their shares.

questions.text: A tax imposed on imported goods is called
questions.explanation: Tariffs raise the price of imports to protect local industry and to generate revenue; quotas restrict quantity instead.

questions.text: Which of the following best measures the standard of living in a country?
questions.explanation: Per capita income relates national income to population size and so reflects average welfare.

questions.text: The main reason why agricultural prices fluctuate sharply is that both demand and supply are
questions.explanation: Inelastic demand and supply mean small shifts in output cause large swings in price.

questions.text: Nigeria's over-dependence on crude oil exports mainly exposes the economy to
questions.explanation: When a single commodity dominates exports, swings in world prices are transmitted directly to government revenue.

questions.text: The transfer of ownership of a government-owned enterprise to private individuals is known as
questions.explanation: Privatisation sells equity to private owners, while commercialisation keeps ownership but requires commercial operation.
